svg.aria-label: Animated diagram: WAL entries are appended and fsynced, become Persisted when a memtable flush writes their keys to an SSTable, and whole segments are deleted by WAL GC once every entry is Persisted; the active segment is never deleted.
svg.text: Every write is fsynced into one shared log. Once a flush has put its keys in an SSTable, WAL GC can delete the segment.
Inserted: only the WAL holds it

g.text: put() appends entry 1 to wal.log and fsyncs before returning.
More writes append to the same segment. Each is fsynced on its own.
Every entry is Inserted: the WAL is the only durable copy of these writes.
The next write opens wal.log.seg000001, which becomes the active segment.
Nothing can be reclaimed yet: every entry is still needed for crash recovery.
A memtable flush writes these keys to an SSTable, so their entries become Persisted.
WAL GC deletes wal.log: every entry in it is Persisted and it is not the active segment.
New writes keep appending to the active segment.
seg000001 is full again, holding a mix of Persisted and Inserted entries.
GC finds nothing to delete: seg000001 still has Inserted entries, and seg000002 is active.
The next flush persists the remaining entries.
GC deletes seg000001. The active segment is never deleted, even when all of it is Persisted.

svg.text: ENTRIES IN WAL FILES ON DISK, AFTER EACH STEP
Illustrative: 4 entries per segment; real segments are 64 MB. With field indexes, GC also waits until each index has checkpointed past a segment.
